title: QRÖMELIFE
excerpt: Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, his third solo album, a 14-track record developed with Pharrell Williams over more than a year and a half.
body:
Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, his third solo album, a 14-track record developed with Pharrell Williams over more than a year and a half. It follows 2023's *Rocket Power*, but comes from a different point in his life. The grief surrounding Takeoff's death is still present, only now it sits beside reconciliation, fatherhood and a project built to move rather than remain in one emotional place.

Sessions moved between Louis Vuitton's headquarters in Paris and a yacht in Miami. Pharrell's role extended across the project, with the two working closely enough that the collaboration became part of its identity rather than a name added at the end. The aim was to bring several sides of Quavo's music into the same room, including the melodic phrasing that became central to Migos, the Atlanta rhythms underneath it and the experiments that had often appeared on features or isolated solo tracks.

The title comes from his idea of a "qrome" state. He uses the word for the point at which pressure, loss and difficult experiences become part of how a person carries himself instead of something that can simply be erased. That idea separates *QRÖMELIFE* from *Rocket Power*. The earlier release was made much closer to Takeoff's death. This one keeps that history in view while allowing the music to look further outward.

[apple:album:6817200688]

The strongest link back to Migos arrives on "Away," which reunites Quavo and Offset on a new recording after years apart musically. Their return together matters without swallowing the rest of the project. The two have also confirmed that they are working on another Migos project intended to honor Takeoff, but no release date has been announced. Here, the reunion works as one part of a solo record that already has its own direction.

Fatherhood has changed that direction too. Quavo recently confirmed that he has become a father for the first time and introduced his daughter in a short film tied to the release. He has spoken about the new purpose and motivation she brought into his life. The film moves through older Migos footage, grief, studio work and the new record before ending with father and daughter together, placing that private change beside the public history he is trying to carry forward.

The music itself is noticeably lighter on its feet than *Rocket Power*. "HAAVIN" first surfaced during Pharrell's Louis Vuitton menswear show in Paris, while "Trance (Walk It Down)" pushes further toward the dance floor without dropping the clipped rhythms and melodic delivery associated with Quavo's Atlanta records. Those shifts keep the music moving without turning it into a checklist of styles or guest appearances.

A 16-track extended version followed a day after the standard edition, adding two versions of "HOTEL LOBBY (Unc & Phew)" with Takeoff. The addition folds one of their best-known records into a release otherwise focused on what came next. *QRÖMELIFE* does not try to rebuild Migos or repeat the grief of *Rocket Power*. It catches Quavo at a point where the past is still visible, but no longer the only thing defining the music in front of him.
